13    /// PdfCraft patch: whether a Flate stream with `params` has no predictor, so that
14    /// [`FlateState`] can produce it a piece at a time.
15    pub(crate) fn is_plain(params: &Dict<'_>) -> bool {
16        PredictorParams::from_params(params).predictor == 1
17    }
18    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::object::Dict;
19
20    /// PdfCraft patch: `limit` is the most bytes inflated (see `filter::decode_limit`), and `rows`
21    /// the `/Height` of the image the data is the samples of, if it is (see [`untagged_png_rows`]).
22    pub(crate) fn decode(data: &[u8], params: &Dict<'_>, limit: usize, rows: Option<usize>) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
23        use flate2::read::{DeflateDecoder, ZlibDecoder};
24        use std::io::Read;
25
26        // Read in chunks and never past `limit`, so the buffer doesn't grow past it either.
27        fn read_up_to(mut decoder: impl Read, limit: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
28            let mut result = Vec::new();
29            let mut chunk = vec![0; 64 * 1024];
30            while result.len() < limit {
31                let n = decoder.read(&mut chunk).ok()?;
32                if n == 0 {
33                    break;
34                }
35                let take = n.min(limit - result.len());
36                result.extend_from_slice(chunk.get(..take)?);
37            }
38            Some(result)
39        }
40        let zlib_stream = |data: &[u8]| read_up_to(ZlibDecoder::new(data), limit);
41        let deflate_stream = |data: &[u8]| read_up_to(DeflateDecoder::new(data), limit);
42
43        let decoded = zlib_stream(data).or_else(|| deflate_stream(data)).or_else(|| {
44            warn!("flate stream is broken, decoding with fallback");
45
46            fallback::decode(data, limit)
47        })?;
48        // PdfCraft patch: output cut at the limit is reported, never dropped silently.
49        if decoded.len() >= limit {
50            warn!("flate stream stopped at its decode limit of {limit} bytes");
51        }
52        undo_predictor(decoded, &PredictorParams::from_params(params), rows)
53    }
54
55    #[cfg(any())]
56    pub(crate) fn decode(data: &[u8], params: &Dict<'_>, limit: usize, rows: Option<usize>) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
57        let decoded = fallback::decode(data, limit)?;
58        // PdfCraft patch: output cut at the limit is reported, never dropped silently.
59        if decoded.len() >= limit {
60            warn!("flate stream stopped at its decode limit of {limit} bytes");
61        }
62        undo_predictor(decoded, &PredictorParams::from_params(params), rows)
63    }
64
65    /// PdfCraft patch: the predictor undone, unless the image's rows carry none
66    /// ([`untagged_png_rows`]): the data is then its samples as they are, which is reported.
67    fn undo_predictor(decoded: Vec<u8>, params: &PredictorParams, rows: Option<usize>) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
68        if untagged_png_rows(params, decoded.len(), rows) {
69            warn!("flate image rows carry no PNG predictor tags, read as stored ({} rows)", rows.unwrap_or(0));
70            return Some(decoded);
71        }
72        apply_predictor(decoded, params)
73    }

75    /// Ported from <https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/master/src/core/flate_stream.js>
76    /// TODO: Rewrite this in idiomatic Rust.
77    mod fallback {
78        use alloc::vec;
79        use alloc::vec::Vec;
80
81        pub(crate) fn decode(data: &[u8], limit: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
82            flate_decode(data, limit)
83        }
84
85        fn flate_decode(data: &[u8], limit: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
86            let mut state = FlateState::new(data);
87            let mut output = Vec::new();
88            state.decode_into(data, &mut output, limit);
89
90            Some(output)
91        }
92
93        /// PdfCraft patch: where a Flate stream is between two calls of [`FlateState::decode_into`].
94        /// Decoding pauses at any output size and resumes where it stopped, so a stream can be
95        /// produced a piece at a time without holding all of it.
96        #[derive(Default)]
97        pub(crate) struct FlateState {
98            pos: usize,
99            code_buf: u32,
100            code_size: u8,
101            eof: bool,
102            block: Block,
103            /// The last `WINDOW` bytes decoded: back-references copy from them, whatever the caller
104            /// has done with the bytes it was given.
105            history: Vec<u8>,
106            /// How many bytes have been decoded in all.
107            total: usize,
108        }
109
110        /// The furthest a Flate back-reference reaches: the largest distance in `DIST_DECODE`.
111        const WINDOW: usize = 32 << 10;
112
113        impl FlateState {
114            /// The state at the start of `data`, past a zlib header if it has one.
115            pub(crate) fn new(data: &[u8]) -> Self {
116                let pos = match data {
117                    [cmf, flg, ..] if (cmf & 0x0f) == 0x08 && (u16::from(*cmf) << 8 | u16::from(*flg)).is_multiple_of(31) && (flg & 0x20) == 0 => 2,
118                    _ => 0,
119                };
120
121                Self { pos, ..Self::default() }
122            }
123
124            /// Whether nothing more can be decoded from `data`.
125            pub(crate) fn finished(&self, data: &[u8]) -> bool {
126                self.eof || (matches!(self.block, Block::Header) && self.pos >= data.len())
127            }
128
129            /// Appends decoded bytes to `out` until it holds `until` bytes or the stream ends.
130            /// `data` is the whole encoded stream, the same on every call.
131            pub(crate) fn decode_into(&mut self, data: &[u8], out: &mut Vec<u8>, until: usize) {
132                // The working buffer is the history followed by the bytes decoded now. Only the
133                // latter go to `out`, which the caller may have drained since.
134                let base = self.history.len();
135                let mut stream = FlateStream {
136                    data,
137                    pos: self.pos,
138                    code_buf: self.code_buf,
139                    code_size: self.code_size,
140                    output: core::mem::take(&mut self.history),
141                    base,
142                    total: self.total,
143                    eof: self.eof,
144                    limit: base.saturating_add(until.saturating_sub(out.len())),
145                    block: core::mem::take(&mut self.block),
146                };
147                stream.run();
148
149                out.extend_from_slice(stream.output.get(base..).unwrap_or(&[]));
150                self.total = self.total.saturating_add(stream.output.len() - base);
151                let keep = stream.output.len().min(WINDOW);
152                stream.output.drain(..stream.output.len() - keep);
153                self.history = stream.output;
154
155                self.pos = stream.pos;
156                self.code_buf = stream.code_buf;
157                self.code_size = stream.code_size;
158                self.eof = stream.eof;
159                self.block = stream.block;
160            }
161        }
162
163        /// PdfCraft patch: the working state of one [`FlateState::decode_into`] call.
164        struct FlateStream<'a> {
165            data: &'a [u8],
166            pos: usize,
167            code_buf: u32,
168            code_size: u8,
169            /// The history, then the bytes decoded in this call.
170            output: Vec<u8>,
171            /// How many bytes of `output` are history.
172            base: usize,
173            /// How many bytes were decoded before this call.
174            total: usize,
175            eof: bool,
176            /// PdfCraft patch: the most bytes in `output` (see `filter::decode_limit`).
177            limit: usize,
178            block: Block,
179        }
180
181        /// PdfCraft patch: the block a Flate stream is in.
182        #[derive(Default)]
183        enum Block {
184            /// Between blocks, at a block header (or at the end of the data).
185            #[default]
186            Header,
187            /// Inside a stored block, with `left` bytes still to copy.
188            Stored { left: usize, last: bool },
189            /// Inside a block coded with Huffman tables. `copy` is a back-reference that the limit
190            /// cut off, as (whether its source exists, distance, bytes left to copy).
191            Coded { lit: HuffmanTable, dist: HuffmanTable, last: bool, copy: Option<(bool, usize, usize)> },
192        }
193
194        impl FlateStream<'_> {
195            /// Decodes until `output` holds `limit` bytes or the stream ends.
196            fn run(&mut self) {
197                loop {
198                    if self.eof || self.output.len() >= self.limit {
199                        return;
200                    }
201
202                    match self.block {
203                        Block::Header => {
204                            if self.pos >= self.data.len() {
205                                return;
206                            }
207
208                            self.read_block();
209                        }
210                        Block::Stored { .. } => self.copy_stored(),
211                        Block::Coded { .. } => self.read_codes(),
212                    }
213                }
214            }
215
216            fn get_byte(&mut self) -> Option<u8> {
217                if self.pos >= self.data.len() {
218                    None
219                } else {
220                    let byte = self.data[self.pos];
221                    self.pos += 1;
222                    Some(byte)
223                }
224            }
225
226            fn peek_byte(&self) -> Option<u8> {
227                if self.pos >= self.data.len() { None } else { Some(self.data[self.pos]) }
228            }
229
230            fn get_bits(&mut self, bits: u8) -> Option<u32> {
231                while self.code_size < bits {
232                    let b = self.get_byte()?;
233                    self.code_buf |= (b as u32) << self.code_size;
234                    self.code_size += 8;
235                }
236
237                let result = self.code_buf & ((1 << bits) - 1);
238                self.code_buf >>= bits;
239                self.code_size -= bits;
240
241                Some(result)
242            }
243
244            fn get_code(&mut self, table: &HuffmanTable) -> Option<u16> {
245                let codes = &table.codes;
246                let max_len = table.max_len;
247
248                while self.code_size < max_len {
249                    if let Some(b) = self.get_byte() {
250                        self.code_buf |= (b as u32) << self.code_size;
251                        self.code_size += 8;
252                    } else {
253                        // Premature end of stream
254                        break;
255                    }
256                }
257
258                let code = codes.get((self.code_buf & ((1 << max_len) - 1)) as usize)?;
259                let code_len = (code >> 16) as u8;
260                let code_val = code & 0xffff;
261
262                if code_len < 1 || self.code_size < code_len {
263                    return None;
264                }
265
266                self.code_buf >>= code_len;
267                self.code_size -= code_len;
268
269                Some(code_val as u16)
270            }
271
272            fn read_block(&mut self) {
273                // Read block header
274                let hdr = match self.get_bits(3) {
275                    Some(h) => h,
276                    None => {
277                        warn!("bad block header in flate stream");
278                        self.eof = true;
279                        return;
280                    }
281                };
282
283                // PdfCraft patch: the final block ends the stream once it is decoded, not when its
284                // header is read: a stored block still has its bytes to copy.
285                let last = (hdr & 1) != 0;
286
287                let hdr = hdr >> 1;
288
289                match hdr {
290                    0 => self.start_uncompressed_block(last),
291                    1 => self.start_compressed_block(true, last),
292                    2 => self.start_compressed_block(false, last),
293                    _ => {
294                        warn!("unknown block type in flate stream");
295                        self.eof = true;
296                    }
297                }
298            }
299
300            fn start_uncompressed_block(&mut self, last: bool) {
301                // Skip any remaining bits in current byte
302                self.code_buf = 0;
303                self.code_size = 0;
304
305                let len_low = match self.get_byte() {
306                    Some(b) => b as u16,
307                    None => {
308                        warn!("bad block header in flate stream");
309                        self.eof = true;
310                        return;
311                    }
312                };
313
314                let len_high = match self.get_byte() {
315                    Some(b) => b as u16,
316                    None => {
317                        warn!("bad block header in flate stream");
318                        self.eof = true;
319                        return;
320                    }
321                };
322
323                let block_len = len_low | (len_high << 8);
324
325                let nlen_low = match self.get_byte() {
326                    Some(b) => b as u16,
327                    None => {
328                        warn!("bad block header in flate stream");
329                        self.eof = true;
330                        return;
331                    }
332                };
333
334                let nlen_high = match self.get_byte() {
335                    Some(b) => b as u16,
336                    None => {
337                        warn!("bad block header in flate stream");
338                        self.eof = true;
339                        return;
340                    }
341                };
342
343                let check = nlen_low | (nlen_high << 8);
344
345                if check != !block_len && (block_len != 0 || check != 0) {
346                    // Ignoring error for bad "empty" block
347                    warn!("bad uncompressed block length in flate stream");
348                }
349
350                if block_len == 0 {
351                    if last || self.peek_byte().is_none() {
352                        self.eof = true;
353                    }
354                } else {
355                    self.block = Block::Stored { left: usize::from(block_len), last };
356                }
357            }
358
359            /// Copies the stored block's bytes, up to the limit or the end of the data.
360            fn copy_stored(&mut self) {
361                let Block::Stored { mut left, last } = self.block else {
362                    return;
363                };
364
365                while left > 0 && self.output.len() < self.limit {
366                    let rest = self.data.get(self.pos..).unwrap_or(&[]);
367                    if rest.is_empty() {
368                        // Premature end of stream: the rest of the block is missing.
369                        self.eof = true;
370                        return;
371                    }
372
373                    let take = left.min(rest.len()).min(self.limit - self.output.len());
374                    self.output.extend_from_slice(rest.get(..take).unwrap_or(&[]));
375                    self.pos += take;
376                    left -= take;
377                }
378
379                if left > 0 {
380                    self.block = Block::Stored { left, last };
381                } else {
382                    self.block = Block::Header;
383                    if last {
384                        self.eof = true;
385                    }
386                }
387            }
388
389            fn start_compressed_block(&mut self, fixed: bool, last: bool) {
390                let (lit_code_table, dist_code_table) = if fixed {
391                    (get_fixed_lit_table(), get_fixed_dist_table())
392                } else {
393                    match self.read_dynamic_tables() {
394                        Some(tables) => tables,
395                        None => {
396                            self.eof = true;
397                            return;
398                        }
399                    }
400                };
401
402                self.block = Block::Coded { lit: lit_code_table, dist: dist_code_table, last, copy: None };
403            }
404
405            /// Decodes the codes of a Huffman-coded block until its end, the limit or the end of
406            /// the data.
407            fn read_codes(&mut self) {
408                let Block::Coded { lit: lit_code_table, dist: dist_code_table, last, mut copy } = core::mem::take(&mut self.block) else {
409                    return;
410                };
411
412                loop {
413                    if let Some((valid, distance, left)) = copy {
414                        let left = self.copy_back(valid, distance, left);
415                        if left > 0 {
416                            // The limit cut the copy short: it resumes on the next call.
417                            self.block = Block::Coded { lit: lit_code_table, dist: dist_code_table, last, copy: Some((valid, distance, left)) };
418                            return;
419                        }
420                        copy = None;
421                    }
422
423                    // PdfCraft patch: one code adds at most 258 bytes; stop at the limit.
424                    if self.output.len() >= self.limit {
425                        self.block = Block::Coded { lit: lit_code_table, dist: dist_code_table, last, copy };
426                        return;
427                    }
428
429                    let code1 = match self.get_code(&lit_code_table) {
430                        Some(c) => c,
431                        None => {
432                            self.eof = true;
433                            return;
434                        }
435                    };
436
437                    if code1 < 256 {
438                        self.output.push(code1 as u8);
439                    } else if code1 == 256 {
440                        if last {
441                            self.eof = true;
442                        }
443                        return;
444                    } else {
445                        let code1 = code1 - 257;
446                        let length_info = LENGTH_DECODE.get(code1 as usize).copied().unwrap_or(0);
447                        let extra_bits = (length_info >> 16) as u8;
448                        let mut length = (length_info & 0xffff) as usize;
449
450                        if extra_bits > 0 {
451                            if let Some(extra) = self.get_bits(extra_bits) {
452                                length += extra as usize;
453                            } else {
454                                self.eof = true;
455                                return;
456                            }
457                        }
458
459                        let dist_code = match self.get_code(&dist_code_table) {
460                            Some(c) => c,
461                            None => {
462                                self.eof = true;
463                                return;
464                            }
465                        };
466
467                        let dist_info = match DIST_DECODE.get(dist_code as usize) {
468                            Some(&info) => info,
469                            None => {
470                                warn!("invalid distance code {} in flate stream", dist_code);
471
472                                self.eof = true;
473                                return;
474                            }
475                        };
476
477                        let extra_bits = (dist_info >> 16) as u8;
478                        let mut distance = (dist_info & 0xffff) as usize;
479
480                        if extra_bits > 0 {
481                            if let Some(extra) = self.get_bits(extra_bits) {
482                                distance += extra as usize;
483                            } else {
484                                self.eof = true;
485                                return;
486                            }
487                        }
488
489                        // Copy from previous output. As before, a distance reaching before the first
490                        // byte decoded copies nothing.
491                        let decoded = self.total.saturating_add(self.output.len().saturating_sub(self.base));
492                        let valid = distance > 0 && distance <= decoded;
493                        copy = Some((valid, distance, length));
494                    }
495                }
496            }
497
498            /// Copies `left` bytes from `distance` back in the output, up to the limit. Returns how
499            /// many are still to copy. A copy whose source does not exist writes nothing.
500            fn copy_back(&mut self, valid: bool, distance: usize, left: usize) -> usize {
501                let len = self.output.len();
502                // Without a source the copy writes nothing, and it runs out only at the limit.
503                let Some(mut start) = len.checked_sub(distance).filter(|_| valid && distance > 0) else {
504                    return if len < self.limit { 0 } else { left };
505                };
506                // PdfCraft patch: copy in runs of up to `distance` bytes. Each run reads only bytes
507                // already in the output, so the bytes are the ones a byte-at-a-time copy writes.
508                let copy = left.min(self.limit.saturating_sub(len));
509                let mut done = 0;
510                while done < copy {
511                    let end = start.saturating_add((copy - done).min(distance));
512                    if end > self.output.len() {
513                        break;
514                    }
515                    self.output.extend_from_within(start..end);
516                    done += end - start;
517                    start = end;
518                }
519
520                left - done
521            }
522
523            fn read_dynamic_tables(&mut self) -> Option<(HuffmanTable, HuffmanTable)> {
524                let num_lit_codes = self.get_bits(5)? as usize + 257;
525                let num_dist_codes = self.get_bits(5)? as usize + 1;
526                let num_code_len_codes = self.get_bits(4)? as usize + 4;
527
528                // Build code length code table
529                let mut code_len_code_lengths = vec![0_u8; 19];
530                for i in 0..num_code_len_codes {
531                    code_len_code_lengths[CODE_LEN_CODE_MAP[i] as usize] = self.get_bits(3)? as u8;
532                }
533
534                let code_len_table = generate_huffman_table(&code_len_code_lengths);
535
536                // Read code lengths
537                let total_codes = num_lit_codes + num_dist_codes;
538                let mut code_lengths = vec![0_u8; total_codes];
539                let mut i = 0;
540
541                while i < total_codes {
542                    let code = self.get_code(&code_len_table)?;
543
544                    match code {
545                        0..=15 => {
546                            code_lengths[i] = code as u8;
547                            i += 1;
548                        }
549                        16 => {
550                            // Repeat previous
551                            let repeat_count = self.get_bits(2)? as usize + 3;
552                            let prev = if i > 0 { code_lengths[i - 1] } else { 0 };
553                            for _ in 0..repeat_count {
554                                if i < total_codes {
555                                    code_lengths[i] = prev;
556                                    i += 1;
557                                }
558                            }
559                        }
560                        17 => {
561                            // Repeat zero 3-10 times
562                            let repeat_count = self.get_bits(3)? as usize + 3;
563                            for _ in 0..repeat_count {
564                                if i < total_codes {
565                                    code_lengths[i] = 0;
566                                    i += 1;
567                                }
568                            }
569                        }
570                        18 => {
571                            // Repeat zero 11-138 times
572                            let repeat_count = self.get_bits(7)? as usize + 11;
573                            for _ in 0..repeat_count {
574                                if i < total_codes {
575                                    code_lengths[i] = 0;
576                                    i += 1;
577                                }
578                            }
579                        }
580                        _ => return None,
581                    }
582                }
583
584                let lit_table = generate_huffman_table(&code_lengths[..num_lit_codes]);
585                let dist_table = generate_huffman_table(&code_lengths[num_lit_codes..]);
586
587                Some((lit_table, dist_table))
588            }
589        }
590
591        struct HuffmanTable {
592            codes: Vec<u32>,
593            max_len: u8,
594        }
595
596        fn generate_huffman_table(lengths: &[u8]) -> HuffmanTable {
597            let _n = lengths.len();
598
599            // Find max code length
600            let max_len = lengths.iter().cloned().max().unwrap_or(0);
601
602            if max_len == 0 {
603                return HuffmanTable { codes: vec![0; 1], max_len: 1 };
604            }
605
606            // Build the table
607            let size = 1 << max_len;
608            let mut codes = vec![0_u32; size];
609
610            let mut code = 0_u32;
611            for len in 1..=max_len {
612                for (val, &length) in lengths.iter().enumerate() {
613                    if length == len {
614                        // Bit-reverse the code
615                        let mut code2 = 0_u32;
616                        let mut t = code;
617                        for _ in 0..len {
618                            code2 = (code2 << 1) | (t & 1);
619                            t >>= 1;
620                        }
621
622                        // Fill the table entries
623                        let skip = 1 << len;
624                        let mut i = code2 as usize;
625                        while i < size {
626                            codes[i] = ((len as u32) << 16) | (val as u32);
627                            i += skip;
628                        }
629                        code += 1;
630                    }
631                }
632                code <<= 1;
633            }
634
635            HuffmanTable { codes, max_len }
636        }
637
638        fn get_fixed_lit_table() -> HuffmanTable {
639            HuffmanTable { codes: FIXED_LIT_CODE_TAB.to_vec(), max_len: 9 }
640        }
641
642        fn get_fixed_dist_table() -> HuffmanTable {
643            HuffmanTable { codes: FIXED_DIST_CODE_TAB.to_vec(), max_len: 5 }
644        }
645
646        const CODE_LEN_CODE_MAP: [u8; 19] = [16, 17, 18, 0, 8, 7, 9, 6, 10, 5, 11, 4, 12, 3, 13, 2, 14, 1, 15];

648        const LENGTH_DECODE: [u32; 29] = [

704pub(crate) mod lzw {
705    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::bit_reader::BitReader;
706    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::filter::lzw_flate::{PredictorParams, apply_predictor};
707    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::object::Dict;
708    use alloc::vec;
709    use alloc::vec::Vec;
710
711    /// Decode a LZW-encoded stream. PdfCraft patch: `limit` is the most bytes produced (see
712    /// `filter::decode_limit`); with a full table every 12-bit code can repeat an entry of
713    /// thousands of bytes.
714    pub(crate) fn decode(data: &[u8], params: &Dict<'_>, limit: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
715        let params = PredictorParams::from_params(params);
716
717        let decoded = decode_impl(data, params.early_change, limit)?;
718        // PdfCraft patch: output cut at the limit is reported, never dropped silently.
719        if decoded.len() >= limit {
720            warn!("LZW stream stopped at its decode limit of {limit} bytes");
721        }
722
723        apply_predictor(decoded, &params)
724    }
725
726    const CLEAR_TABLE: usize = 256;
727    const EOD: usize = 257;
728    const MAX_ENTRIES: usize = 4096;
729    const INITIAL_SIZE: u16 = 258;
730
731    fn decode_impl(data: &[u8], early_change: bool, limit: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
732        let mut table = Table::new(early_change);
733        let mut bit_size = table.code_length();
734        let mut reader = BitReader::new(data);
735        let mut decoded = vec![];
736        let mut prev = None;
737
738        loop {
739            if decoded.len() >= limit {
740                return Some(decoded);
741            }
742            let next = match reader.read(bit_size) {
743                Some(code) => code as usize,
744                None => {
745                    warn!("premature EOF in LZW stream, EOD code missing");
746                    return Some(decoded);
747                }
748            };
749
750            match next {
751                CLEAR_TABLE => {
752                    table.clear();
753                    prev = None;
754                    bit_size = table.code_length();
755                }
756                EOD => return Some(decoded),
757                new => {
758                    if new > table.size() {
759                        warn!("invalid LZW code: {} (table size: {})", new, table.size());
760                        return None;
761                    }
762
763                    // PdfCraft patch: never past `limit`.
764                    let left = limit.saturating_sub(decoded.len());
765                    if new < table.size() {
766                        let entry = table.get(new)?;
767                        let first_byte = entry[0];
768                        decoded.extend_from_slice(entry.get(..entry.len().min(left))?);
769
770                        if let Some(prev_code) = prev {
771                            table.register(prev_code, first_byte);
772                        }
773                    } else if new == table.size() && prev.is_some() {
774                        let prev_code = prev.unwrap();
775                        let prev_entry = table.get(prev_code)?;
776                        let first_byte = prev_entry[0];
777
778                        let new_entry = table.register(prev_code, first_byte)?;
779                        decoded.extend_from_slice(new_entry.get(..new_entry.len().min(left))?);
780                    } else {
781                        warn!("LZW decode error: code {new} not found and prev is None");
782                        return None;
783                    }
784
785                    bit_size = table.code_length();
786                    prev = Some(new);
787                }
788            }
789        }
790    }
791
792    struct Table {
793        early_change: bool,
794        entries: Vec<Option<Vec<u8>>>,
795    }
796
797    impl Table {
798        fn new(early_change: bool) -> Self {
799            let mut entries: Vec<_> = (0..=255).map(|b| Some(vec![b])).collect();
800
801            // Clear table and EOD don't have any data.
802            entries.push(None); // 256 = CLEAR_TABLE
803            entries.push(None); // 257 = EOD
804
805            Self { early_change, entries }
806        }
807
808        fn push(&mut self, entry: Vec<u8>) -> Option<&[u8]> {
809            if self.entries.len() >= MAX_ENTRIES {
810                None
811            } else {
812                self.entries.push(Some(entry));
813                self.entries.last()?.as_ref().map(|v| &**v)
814            }
815        }
816
817        fn register(&mut self, prev: usize, new_byte: u8) -> Option<&[u8]> {
818            let prev_entry = self.get(prev)?;
819
820            let mut new_entry = Vec::with_capacity(prev_entry.len() + 1);
821            new_entry.extend(prev_entry);
822            new_entry.push(new_byte);
823            self.push(new_entry)
824        }
825
826        fn get(&self, index: usize) -> Option<&[u8]> {
827            self.entries.get(index)?.as_ref().map(|v| &**v)
828        }
829
830        fn clear(&mut self) {
831            self.entries.truncate(INITIAL_SIZE as usize);
832        }
833
834        fn size(&self) -> usize {
835            self.entries.len()
836        }
837
838        fn code_length(&self) -> u8 {
839            const TEN: usize = 512;
840            const ELEVEN: usize = 1024;
841            const TWELVE: usize = 2048;
842
843            let adjusted = self.entries.len() + (if self.early_change { 1 } else { 0 });
844
845            if adjusted >= TWELVE {
846                12
847            } else if adjusted >= ELEVEN {
848                11
849            } else if adjusted >= TEN {
850                10
851            } else {
852                9
853            }
854        }
855    }
856}
857
858struct PredictorParams {
859    predictor: u8,
860    colors: u8,
861    bits_per_component: u8,
862    columns: usize,
863    early_change: bool,
864}
865
866impl PredictorParams {
867    fn row_length_in_bytes(&self) -> usize {
868        // PdfCraft patch: saturating, and in usize (colors × bits overflowed u8): a fuzzed
869        // `/Columns 9223372036854775807` wrapped to a 2^61-byte row.
870        self.columns.saturating_mul(usize::from(self.bits_per_component) * usize::from(self.colors)).div_ceil(8)
871    }
872}
873
874impl Default for PredictorParams {
875    fn default() -> Self {
876        Self { predictor: 1, colors: 1, bits_per_component: 8, columns: 1, early_change: true }
877    }
878}
879
880impl PredictorParams {
881    fn from_params(dict: &Dict<'_>) -> Self {
882        Self {
883            predictor: dict.get(PREDICTOR).unwrap_or(1),
884            colors: dict.get(COLORS).unwrap_or(1),
885            bits_per_component: dict.get(BITS_PER_COMPONENT).unwrap_or(8),
886            columns: dict.get(COLUMNS).unwrap_or(1),
887            early_change: dict.get::<u8>(EARLY_CHANGE).map(|e| e != 0).unwrap_or(true),
888        }
889    }
890}
891
892/// PdfCraft patch: whether `len` bytes of an image `rows` high (`None` for data that isn't an
893/// image's samples) are its rows without the filter-type byte each row starts with under a PNG
894/// predictor (ISO 32000-2 §7.4.4.4): exactly `rows` × the row's bytes, where the predicted data
895/// would be `rows` × (the row's bytes + 1). Some writers declare `/Predictor 15` without applying
896/// it; read with the predictor, every row's first byte was taken for a filter type, the image
897/// shifted a byte a row and came out short, drawn in fragments. PDFium, MuPDF and Poppler read
898/// such data as the samples it is. Any other length is decoded with the predictor, as before.
899fn untagged_png_rows(params: &PredictorParams, len: usize, rows: Option<usize>) -> bool {
900    let row_len = params.row_length_in_bytes();
901    params.predictor >= 10
902        && matches!(params.bits_per_component, 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16)
903        && row_len > 0
904        && rows.filter(|&r| r > 0).and_then(|r| r.checked_mul(row_len)) == Some(len)
905}
906
907fn apply_predictor(data: Vec<u8>, params: &PredictorParams) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
908    match params.predictor {
909        1 => Some(data),
910        i => {
911            let is_png_predictor = i >= 10;
912
913            let row_len = params.row_length_in_bytes();
914
915            let total_row_len = if is_png_predictor {
916                // + 1 Because each row must start with the predictor that is used for PNG predictors.
917                row_len.saturating_add(1)
918            } else {
919                row_len
920            };
921
922            // PdfCraft patch: a zero-width row divided by zero below, and a row longer than the
923            // data was allocated before finding there is nothing to read (no rows: empty output,
924            // as before).
925            if row_len == 0 {
926                return None;
927            }
928            if total_row_len > data.len() {
929                return Some(Vec::new());
930            }
931
932            let num_rows = data.len() / total_row_len;
933
934            if !matches!(params.bits_per_component, 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16) {
935                warn!("invalid bits per component {}", params.bits_per_component);
936
937                return None;
938            }
939
940            if is_png_predictor {
941                // PdfCraft patch: PNG predictors work on bytes whatever the bit depth, so they are
942                // undone a row at a time on byte slices instead of through the bit-level readers.
943                // In usize (the u8 product overflowed).
944                let bpp = (usize::from(params.colors) * usize::from(params.bits_per_component)).div_ceil(8);
945                return Some(unfilter_png(&data, row_len, bpp));
946            }
947
948            if i == 2 && matches!(params.bits_per_component, 8 | 16) && !bit_level_only() {
949                // PdfCraft patch: whole-byte samples are undone a row at a time on byte slices
950                // instead of through the bit-level readers, which packed samples need.
951                let sample_len = usize::from(params.bits_per_component / 8);
952                let pixel_len = usize::from(params.colors).saturating_mul(sample_len);
953                return Some(undo_tiff_bytes(data, row_len, pixel_len, sample_len));
954            }
955
956            #[cfg(any())]
957            BIT_LEVEL_TIFF_ROWS.with(|rows| rows.set(rows.get().saturating_add(num_rows)));
958
959            let (bit_size, chunk_len) = (params.bits_per_component, params.colors as usize);
960            let zero_row = vec![0; row_len];
961            let mut prev_row = BitChunks::new(&zero_row, bit_size, chunk_len)?;
962            let zero_col = BitChunk::new(0, chunk_len);
963            let mut out = vec![0; num_rows * row_len];
964            let mut writer = BitWriter::new(&mut out, bit_size)?;
965
966            for in_row in data.chunks_exact(total_row_len) {
967                if i == 2 {
968                    apply::<Sub>(
969                        prev_row,
970                        zero_col.clone(),
971                        zero_col.clone(),
972                        BitChunks::new(in_row, bit_size, chunk_len)?,
973                        &mut writer,
974                        chunk_len,
975                        bit_size,
976                    );
977                } else {
978                    warn!("unknown predictor {i}");
979
980                    return None;
981                }
982
983                // PdfCraft patch: packed TIFF samples can leave padding bits at the end
984                // of a row. split_off requires byte alignment or the next row overwrites it.
985                writer.align();
986                let (data, new_writer) = writer.split_off();
987                writer = new_writer;
988                prev_row = BitChunks::new(data, bit_size, chunk_len)?;
989            }
990
991            Some(out)
992        }
993    }
994}
995
996/// PdfCraft patch: undoes TIFF predictor 2 (ISO 32000-2 §7.4.4.4, Table 10; TIFF 6.0 §14)
997/// for 8- and 16-bit samples, in rows of `row_len` bytes holding pixels of `pixel_len` bytes,
998/// each sample `sample_len` bytes (1 or 2, big-endian): every sample is added to the same
999/// component of the pixel to its left, wrapping at the sample's width. Bytes after the last
1000/// complete row are dropped, as the bit-level path drops them.
1001fn undo_tiff_bytes(mut data: Vec<u8>, row_len: usize, pixel_len: usize, sample_len: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
1002    let num_rows = data.len() / row_len.max(1);
1003    data.truncate(num_rows.saturating_mul(row_len));
1004    if pixel_len == 0 {
1005        return data;
1006    }
1007
1008    for row in data.chunks_exact_mut(row_len) {
1009        let mut pixels = row.chunks_exact_mut(pixel_len);
1010        let Some(mut left) = pixels.next() else {
1011            continue;
1012        };
1013        for px in pixels {
1014            if sample_len == 2 {
1015                for (c, l) in px.chunks_exact_mut(2).zip(left.chunks_exact(2)) {
1016                    if let ([c0, c1], [l0, l1]) = (c, l) {
1017                        let sum = u16::from_be_bytes([*c0, *c1]).wrapping_add(u16::from_be_bytes([*l0, *l1]));
1018                        [*c0, *c1] = sum.to_be_bytes();
1019                    }
1020                }
1021            } else {
1022                for (c, l) in px.iter_mut().zip(left.iter()) {
1023                    *c = c.wrapping_add(*l);
1024                }
1025            }
1026            left = px;
1027        }
1028    }
1029
1030    data
1031}

1033#[cfg(any())]
1034std::thread_local! {
1035    /// PdfCraft patch tests: rows the bit-level TIFF predictor path has undone on this thread.
1036    static BIT_LEVEL_TIFF_ROWS: core::cell::Cell<usize> = const { core::cell::Cell::new(0) };
1037    /// PdfCraft patch tests: send whole-byte TIFF samples through the bit-level path too.
1038    static BIT_LEVEL_ONLY: core::cell::Cell<bool> = const { core::cell::Cell::new(false) };

1052/// PdfCraft patch: undoes PNG row filters (ISO 32000-2 §7.4.4.4, PNG specification §9) in
1053/// rows of `row_len` bytes, each after its filter-type byte, with `bpp` bytes per complete pixel
1054/// (at least 1). An unknown filter type copies the row as it is. Bytes after the last complete
1055/// row are dropped.
1056fn unfilter_png(data: &[u8], row_len: usize, bpp: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
1057    let bpp = bpp.max(1);
1058    let in_row_len = row_len.saturating_add(1);
1059    let num_rows = data.len() / in_row_len;
1060    let mut out = vec![0; num_rows.saturating_mul(row_len)];
1061    let zero_row = vec![0; row_len];
1062    let mut prev: &[u8] = &zero_row;
1063
1064    for (cur, in_row) in out.chunks_exact_mut(row_len).zip(data.chunks_exact(in_row_len)) {
1065        let Some((&filter, src)) = in_row.split_first() else {
1066            break;
1067        };
1068
1069        match filter {
1070            1 => {
1071                let mut left: &[u8] = &zero_row;
1072                for (px, src) in cur.chunks_mut(bpp).zip(src.chunks(bpp)) {
1073                    for ((c, s), l) in px.iter_mut().zip(src).zip(left) {
1074                        *c = s.wrapping_add(*l);
1075                    }
1076                    left = px;
1077                }
1078            }
1079            2 => {
1080                for ((c, s), u) in cur.iter_mut().zip(src).zip(prev) {
1081                    *c = s.wrapping_add(*u);
1082                }
1083            }
1084            3 => {
1085                let mut left: &[u8] = &zero_row;
1086                for ((px, src), up) in cur.chunks_mut(bpp).zip(src.chunks(bpp)).zip(prev.chunks(bpp)) {
1087                    for (((c, s), l), u) in px.iter_mut().zip(src).zip(left).zip(up) {
1088                        // The sum is taken before halving, without wrapping.
1089                        let avg = (u16::from(*l) + u16::from(*u)) / 2;
1090                        *c = s.wrapping_add(avg as u8);
1091                    }
1092                    left = px;
1093                }
1094            }
1095            4 => {
1096                let mut left: &[u8] = &zero_row;
1097                let mut up_left: &[u8] = &zero_row;
1098                for ((px, src), up) in cur.chunks_mut(bpp).zip(src.chunks(bpp)).zip(prev.chunks(bpp)) {
1099                    for ((((c, s), l), u), ul) in px.iter_mut().zip(src).zip(left).zip(up).zip(up_left) {
1100                        *c = s.wrapping_add(paeth_byte(*l, *u, *ul));
1101                    }
1102                    left = px;
1103                    up_left = up;
1104                }
1105            }
1106            _ => {
1107                for (c, s) in cur.iter_mut().zip(src) {
1108                    *c = *s;
1109                }
1110            }
1111        }
1112
1113        prev = cur;
1114    }
1115
1116    out
1117}
1118
1119/// The Paeth predictor on bytes: the neighbour nearest `left + up - up_left`, preferring left,
1120/// then up.
1121fn paeth_byte(left: u8, up: u8, up_left: u8) -> u8 {
1122    let (a, b, c) = (i16::from(left), i16::from(up), i16::from(up_left));
1123    let pa = (b - c).abs();
1124    let pb = (a - c).abs();
1125    let pc = (a + b - c - c).abs();
1126
1127    let not_left = if pb <= pc { up } else { up_left };
1128    if pa <= pb && pa <= pc { left } else { not_left }
1129}
1130
1131fn apply<'a, T: Predictor>(
1132    prev_row: BitChunks<'a>,
1133    mut prev_col: BitChunk,
1134    mut top_left: BitChunk,
1135    cur_row: BitChunks<'a>,
1136    writer: &mut BitWriter<'a>,
1137    chunk_len: usize,
1138    bit_size: u8,
1139) -> Option<()> {
1140    for (cur_row, prev_row) in cur_row.zip(prev_row) {
1141        let old_pos = writer.cur_pos();
1142
1143        for (((cur_row, prev_row), prev_col), top_left) in cur_row.iter().zip(prev_row.iter()).zip(prev_col.iter()).zip(top_left.iter()) {
1144            // Note that the wrapping behavior when adding inside the predictors is dependent on the
1145            // bit size, so it wouldn't be triggered for bits per component < 16. So we mask out
1146            // the bytes manually, which is equivalent to a wrapping add.
1147            writer.write(T::predict(cur_row, prev_row, prev_col, top_left) as u32 & bit_mask(bit_size));
1148        }
1149
1150        prev_col = {
1151            let out_data = writer.get_data();
1152            let mut reader = BitReader::new_with(out_data, old_pos);
1153            BitChunk::from_reader(&mut reader, bit_size, chunk_len).unwrap()
1154        };
1155
1156        top_left = prev_row;
1157    }
1158
1159    Some(())
1160}
1161
1162trait Predictor {
1163    fn predict(cur_row: u16, prev_row: u16, prev_col: u16, top_left: u16) -> u16;
1164}
1165
1166struct Sub;
1167impl Predictor for Sub {
1168    fn predict(cur_row: u16, _: u16, prev_col: u16, _: u16) -> u16 {
1169        cur_row.wrapping_add(prev_col)
1170    }
1171}

1307        ];
1308        let expected = b"abc".repeat(2000);
1309        let mut state = flate::FlateState::new(&ABC_2000);
1310        let mut out = Vec::new();
1311        loop {
1312            let before = out.len();
1313            state.decode_into(&ABC_2000, &mut out, before + 7);
1314            if out.len() == before || out.len() >= expected.len() {
1315                break;
1316            }
1317        }
1318
1319        assert_eq!(out, expected);
1320    }

1338/// PdfCraft patch tests: PNG predictors are undone byte by byte (`unfilter_png`).
1339#[cfg(any())]
1340mod pdfcraft_png_predictor_tests {
1341    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::filter::lzw_flate::{PredictorParams, apply_predictor, flate, untagged_png_rows};
1342    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::object::{Dict, FromBytes};
1343
1344    /// `data` as one stored (uncompressed) deflate block, at most 65,535 bytes.
1345    fn stored(data: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
1346        let len = u16::try_from(data.len()).unwrap();
1347        let mut out = vec![1];
1348        out.extend(len.to_le_bytes());
1349        out.extend((!len).to_le_bytes());
1350        out.extend(data);
1351        out
1352    }
1353
1354    /// `data` inflated and its PNG predictor undone, as the last filter of an image `rows` high.
1355    fn inflate(parms: &[u8], data: &[u8], rows: Option<usize>) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
1356        let parms = Dict::from_bytes(parms).unwrap();
1357        flate::decode(&stored(data), &parms, usize::MAX, rows)
1358    }
1359
1360    const RGB3: &[u8] = b"<< /Predictor 15 /Colors 3 /BitsPerComponent 8 /Columns 3 >>";
1361
1362    #[cfg(any())]
1363    fn an_image_whose_rows_carry_no_png_tags_is_read_as_its_samples() {
1364        // Three RGB pixels a row, four rows: 36 bytes, where the predictor would need 40. Every
1365        // row starts with a byte above 4, which the predictor took for a filter type, so the
1366        // image came out three rows of shifted samples.
1367        let samples: Vec<u8> = (0..36).map(|i| 200 - i as u8).collect();
1368        assert_eq!(inflate(RGB3, &samples, Some(4)).unwrap(), samples);
1369        let params = PredictorParams { predictor: 15, colors: 3, bits_per_component: 8, columns: 3, early_change: false };
1370        assert!(untagged_png_rows(&params, 36, Some(4)), "the repair is reported");
1371        // Not an image's samples (no height known): the predictor is undone, as before.
1372        assert_eq!(inflate(RGB3, &samples, None).unwrap(), apply_predictor(samples.clone(), &params).unwrap());
1373        assert!(!untagged_png_rows(&params, 36, None));
1374    }
1375
1376    #[cfg(any())]
1377    fn an_image_whose_rows_carry_png_tags_still_has_its_predictor_undone() {
1378        // The same four rows, each filtered None, then Sub: 40 bytes.
1379        let samples: Vec<u8> = (0..36).map(|i| 200 - i as u8).collect();
1380        let mut tagged = Vec::new();
1381        for row in samples.chunks(9) {
1382            tagged.push(1);
1383            let mut left = [0u8; 3];
1384            for px in row.chunks(3) {
1385                tagged.extend(px.iter().zip(left).map(|(s, l)| s.wrapping_sub(l)));
1386                left.copy_from_slice(px);
1387            }
1388        }
1389        assert_eq!(tagged.len(), 40);
1390        assert_eq!(inflate(RGB3, &tagged, Some(4)).unwrap(), samples);
1391    }

1396        // Short of the untagged length, past it, or between it and the tagged one.

1399            assert!(!untagged_png_rows(&params, len, Some(4)), "{len} bytes");

1415            let params = PredictorParams { predictor: 15, colors, bits_per_component, columns, early_change: false };

1424        for parms in [&zero[..], &huge[..]] {

1431    /// PNG unfiltering written out from the PNG specification (§9.2–9.4), one byte at a time.
1432    fn reference(data: &[u8], row_len: usize, bpp: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
1433        let mut out: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
1434        for (r, row) in data.chunks_exact(row_len + 1).enumerate() {
1435            let start = r * row_len;
1436            for x in 0..row_len {
1437                let left = if x >= bpp { out[start + x - bpp] } else { 0 };
1438                let up = if r > 0 { out[start + x - row_len] } else { 0 };
1439                let up_left = if r > 0 && x >= bpp { out[start + x - row_len - bpp] } else { 0 };
1440                let predicted = match row[0] {
1441                    1 => left,
1442                    2 => up,
1443                    3 => ((u16::from(left) + u16::from(up)) / 2) as u8,
1444                    4 => {
1445                        let p = i16::from(left) + i16::from(up) - i16::from(up_left);
1446                        let (pa, pb, pc) = ((p - i16::from(left)).abs(), (p - i16::from(up)).abs(), (p - i16::from(up_left)).abs());
1447                        if pa <= pb && pa <= pc {
1448                            left
1449                        } else if pb <= pc {
1450                            up
1451                        } else {
1452                            up_left
1453                        }
1454                    }
1455                    _ => 0,
1456                };
1457                out.push(row[1 + x].wrapping_add(predicted));
1458            }
1459        }
1460        out
1461    }
1462
1463    #[cfg(any())]
1464    fn png_predictors_match_the_specification_at_every_depth_and_pixel_size() {
1465        let mut seed: u32 = 0x2545_f491;
1466        let mut next = move || {
1467            seed ^= seed << 13;
1468            seed ^= seed >> 17;
1469            seed ^= seed << 5;
1470            seed
1471        };
1472        for case in 0..400 {
1473            let colors = 1 + (next() % 4) as u8;
1474            let bits_per_component = [1u8, 2, 4, 8, 16][(next() % 5) as usize];
1475            let columns = 1 + (next() % 40) as usize;
1476            let bpp = (usize::from(colors) * usize::from(bits_per_component)).div_ceil(8);
1477            let row_len = (columns * usize::from(colors) * usize::from(bits_per_component)).div_ceil(8);
1478            let rows = 1 + (next() % 6) as usize;
1479            let mut data = Vec::new();
1480            for _ in 0..rows {
1481                // Filter types 0–4, and 5–7, which are not PNG filters and copy the row.
1482                data.push((next() % 8) as u8);
1483                data.extend((0..row_len).map(|_| next() as u8));
1484            }
1485            // A partial row at the end is not decoded.
1486            let tail = (next() % 3) as usize;
1487            data.extend((0..tail.min(row_len)).map(|_| next() as u8));
1488
1489            let params = PredictorParams { predictor: 10 + (next() % 6) as u8, colors, bits_per_component, columns, early_change: false };
1490            let got = apply_predictor(data.clone(), &params).unwrap();
1491            assert_eq!(got, reference(&data, row_len, bpp), "case {case}: {colors} colours at {bits_per_component} bits, {columns} columns");
1492        }
1493    }

1496    fn a_row_ending_part_way_through_a_pixel_keeps_its_last_byte() {
1497        // Three 4-bit samples are a byte and a half, so a three-column row is five bytes and ends
1498        // half-way through a two-byte pixel. Each row is filtered Up.
1499        let data = [
1500            2, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, //
1501            2, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, //
1502            2, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34,
1503        ];
1504        let params = PredictorParams { predictor: 15, colors: 3, bits_per_component: 4, columns: 3, early_change: false };
1505        assert_eq!(apply_predictor(data.to_vec(), &params).unwrap(), [10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 30, 32, 34, 36, 38, 60, 63, 66, 69, 72]);

1508    #[cfg(any())]
1509    fn png_average_and_paeth_carry_the_left_pixel_across_a_wide_row() {
1510        // Three 16-bit samples (6 bytes) per pixel: the left neighbour is six bytes back.
1511        let row_len = 6 * 3;
1512        let mut data = vec![3u8];
1513        data.extend((0..row_len).map(|i| (i * 37 + 200) as u8));
1514        data.push(4);
1515        data.extend((0..row_len).map(|i| (255 - i * 11) as u8));
1516        let params = PredictorParams { predictor: 15, colors: 3, bits_per_component: 16, columns: 3, early_change: false };
1517        assert_eq!(apply_predictor(data.clone(), &params).unwrap(), reference(&data, row_len, 6));
1518    }

1521/// PdfCraft patch tests: TIFF predictor 2 on 8- and 16-bit samples is undone on byte rows
1522/// (`undo_tiff_bytes`), with the same output as the bit-level path.
1523#[cfg(any())]
1524mod pdfcraft_tiff_predictor_tests {
1525    use super::{BIT_LEVEL_ONLY, BIT_LEVEL_TIFF_ROWS};
1526    use crate::third_party::hayro_syntax::filter::lzw_flate::{PredictorParams, apply_predictor};
1527
1528    fn tiff(colors: u8, bits_per_component: u8, columns: usize) -> PredictorParams {
1529        PredictorParams { predictor: 2, colors, bits_per_component, columns, early_change: false }
1530    }
1531
1532    /// Both paths' output, the byte path's first; `None` from either is kept.
1533    fn both(data: &[u8], params: &PredictorParams) -> (Option<Vec<u8>>, Option<Vec<u8>>) {
1534        let fast = apply_predictor(data.to_vec(), params);
1535        BIT_LEVEL_ONLY.with(|only| only.set(true));
1536        let bits = apply_predictor(data.to_vec(), params);
1537        BIT_LEVEL_ONLY.with(|only| only.set(false));
1538        (fast, bits)
1539    }
1540
1541    #[cfg(any())]
1542    fn whole_byte_samples_match_the_bit_level_path_on_random_rows() {
1543        let mut seed: u32 = 0x9e37_79b9;
1544        let mut next = move || {
1545            seed ^= seed << 13;
1546            seed ^= seed >> 17;
1547            seed ^= seed << 5;
1548            seed
1549        };
1550        for case in 0..600 {
1551            let colors = [1u8, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7][(next() % 6) as usize];
1552            let bits_per_component = [8u8, 16][(next() % 2) as usize];
1553            let columns = 1 + (next() % 50) as usize;
1554            let row_len = columns * usize::from(colors) * usize::from(bits_per_component) / 8;
1555            let rows = (next() % 7) as usize;
1556            // A partial row at the end, or none.
1557            let tail = (next() % 4) as usize % row_len;
1558            let data: Vec<u8> = (0..rows * row_len + tail).map(|_| next() as u8).collect();
1559            let params = tiff(colors, bits_per_component, columns);
1560            let (fast, bits) = both(&data, &params);
1561            assert_eq!(
1562                fast, bits,
1563                "case {case}: {colors} colours at {bits_per_component} bits, {columns} columns,                  {rows} rows and {tail} bytes"
1564            );
1565        }
1566    }
1567
1568    #[cfg(any())]
1569    fn whole_byte_samples_add_to_the_same_component_of_the_pixel_to_their_left() {
1570        // Two 8-bit colours, three columns, two rows; sums wrap at 256.
1571        let data = [10, 20, 1, 2, 3, 4, /* row 2 */ 5, 5, 250, 10, 1, 1];
1572        assert_eq!(apply_predictor(data.to_vec(), &tiff(2, 8, 3)).unwrap(), [10, 20, 11, 22, 14, 26, 5, 5, 255, 15, 0, 16]);
1573        // One 16-bit colour: a carry crosses the byte boundary and the sum wraps at 65,536.
1574        let data = [0x01, 0x00, 0xff, 0xff, 0x00, 0x02, /* row 2 */ 0x00, 0xff, 0x00, 0x01, 0, 0];
1575        assert_eq!(
1576            apply_predictor(data.to_vec(), &tiff(1, 16, 3)).unwrap(),
1577            [0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0xff, 0x01, 0x01, 0x00, 0xff, 0x01, 0x00, 0x01, 0x00]
1578        );
1579    }
1580
1581    #[cfg(any())]
1582    fn whole_byte_samples_do_not_take_the_bit_level_path() {
1583        let start = BIT_LEVEL_TIFF_ROWS.with(core::cell::Cell::get);
1584        for bits_per_component in [8, 16] {
1585            let data = vec![7; 3 * 4 * usize::from(bits_per_component) / 8 * 5];
1586            apply_predictor(data, &tiff(3, bits_per_component, 4)).unwrap();
1587        }
1588        assert_eq!(BIT_LEVEL_TIFF_ROWS.with(core::cell::Cell::get), start);
1589
1590        // Packed samples still do.
1591        apply_predictor(vec![0x5f; 4], &tiff(1, 4, 2)).unwrap();
1592        assert_eq!(BIT_LEVEL_TIFF_ROWS.with(core::cell::Cell::get), start + 4);
1593    }
1594
1595    #[cfg(any())]
1596    fn rows_without_a_complete_row_of_data_are_dropped_on_both_paths() {
1597        for (data, params, want) in [
1598            // Shorter than one row: nothing.
1599            (vec![1, 2, 3], tiff(1, 8, 4), Some(vec![])),
1600            (vec![1, 2, 3], tiff(1, 16, 2), Some(vec![])),
1601            // A zero-width row is refused.
1602            (vec![1, 2, 3], tiff(1, 8, 0), None),
1603            (vec![], tiff(1, 16, 0), None),
1604            // No data at all.
1605            (vec![], tiff(3, 8, 2), Some(vec![])),
1606            // The trailing partial row is dropped.
1607            (vec![1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2], tiff(1, 8, 4), Some(vec![1, 2, 3, 4])),
1608            (vec![0, 1, 0, 1, 9], tiff(1, 16, 2), Some(vec![0, 1, 0, 2])),
1609        ] {
1610            let (fast, bits) = both(&data, &params);
1611            assert_eq!(fast, want, "{data:?}");
1612            assert_eq!(bits, want, "{data:?}");
1613        }
1614    }
1615}
